papers.Abstract: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.
papers.Core_Innovation: Integrates 17 robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified API for improved reusability. Introduces a standardized evaluation platform with 273 perturbation configurations spanning real-world shifts, humanoid and vision-language-action tasks.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Vehicles, Manufacturing
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Rule-Based Control, Simulated-Only Robotics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Mandate RobustRLlib integration for internal RL pipelines within Q3 to harden autonomous systems against distribution shift. Allocate funding to benchmark 17 algorithms against production-grade perturbation suites.
papers.Tags: Robust Reinforcement Learning, Unified Library, Empirical Benchmarking
papers.Hook: Enables systematic robustness mapping for 17 RL algorithms across diverse real-world shifts

papers.Title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
papers.Abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.
papers.Core_Innovation: DexPort records both commanded joint targets and measured states via a hand-held interface, using identical hardware for collection and deployment to eliminate embodiment mismatch. Operators select skill-based finger coordination primitives rather than independently controlling each joint.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Industrial Automation, Prosthetics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Teleoperation Services, Robotics Data Labeling
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund DexPort-inspired data collection pipelines within 12 months to secure dexterous manipulation datasets. Kill legacy teleoperation-dependent data acquisition projects that cannot integrate skill-based coordination.
papers.Tags: dexterous manipulation, data collection, robot hands, skill interface
papers.Hook: Portable interface enables robot hand skills without full teleoperation setups.

papers.Title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
papers.Abstract: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images. Common approaches tie inference to stored exemplars, impose rigid linear structure, or risk reproducing anomalous content. Flownomaly instead casts the problem as normal-counterpart recovery in frozen DINOv2 feature space. Given normal supports, a velocity field is learned through conditional flow matching over frozen patch tokens to transport Gaussian noise toward normal features. Along straight paths, a single recovery step using one evaluation of the optimal field yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without trajectory integration. The operating time governs how strongly recovery modifies a query token. With no anomalous validation samples available for tuning, a normal-only Jacobian gain-to-noise criterion selects this time from the supports alone. Squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered counterparts yield anomaly signals for both dense localization and image-level detection. Across 1-, 2-, and 4-shot benchmarks on MVTec-AD and VisA, together with sample-shot evaluations on Real-IAD, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance against recent category-specific methods. In the 1-shot setting, image- and pixel-level AUROC reach 97.8% and 98.0% on MVTec-AD and 95.3% and 98.7% on VisA, with a 2.1-point image-level AUROC improvement over the strongest baseline on VisA. Code is available at https://github.com/b-rbmp/Flownomaly.
papers.Core_Innovation: Replaces iterative trajectory integration with a single-step optimal velocity field evaluation using conditional flow matching. It introduces a Jacobian gain-to-noise criterion to tune recovery time without anomalous validation data.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Advanced Manufacturing, Semiconductor Fabrication, Quality Assurance
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Manual Inspection Services
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund the integration of this flow-matching architecture into existing DINOv2-based vision pipelines for immediate deployment in low-data factory environments. Buy compute for high-throughput patch-token processing to replace iterative diffusion-based anomaly detectors.
papers.Tags: Few-Shot Learning, Anomaly Detection, Conditional Flow Matching, DINOv2
papers.Hook: Detect industrial defects using few-shot samples via single-step conditional-mean recovery in frozen feature space.

papers.Title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
papers.Abstract: Personal email agents decide, for every message, what it is, whether it is urgent, whether to draft a reply, create a task, or ignore it. Their error rate is rarely measured: the stored labels were written by the system itself. We present Foyer, a self-hosted personal inbox agent in daily use, and a measurement protocol (stratified sampling, frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, pre-registered hypotheses, human labels in the agent's review loop) that yields ground truth before any training. On 739 real Italian/English emails labelled by the owner (231 unbiased, 500 adversarially sampled), we compare nine systems under thread-grouped cross-validation: the production keyword rules, a TF-IDF + logistic-regression baseline, local typed decision models (Tev1, Nimble), a hosted decision model (Nimble v4-max), and hosted generative LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma 4 26B/31B). Four results. The production rules score 28% on message type against a 58% majority class: the field shown most prominently carried no information. With ~200 labels, logistic regression has the highest accuracy on every field (type 0.79, urgency 0.74, needs-reply 0.83, is-noise 0.90), though it never predicts the two rarest classes and is statistically tied with Gemma 4 on type; few-shot prompting does not close the gap. The sender's relationship (client, supplier, service) is recovered from other emails of the same contact with 98.6% accuracy where the contact has been seen, and is not inferable from a single message by any model: it belongs in the contact graph, not the prompt. Finally, accuracy is not the product metric: composed into actions, the most accurate system most often ignores emails needing action (18% vs 4% for the best LLM); a cost-chosen threshold on its noise probability halves that rate and makes it the cheapest system.
papers.Core_Innovation: The core innovation is a pre-training protocol that uses stratified adversarial sampling, frozen snapshots, and thread-grouped splits to generate human-verified ground truth before any model training
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Email Services, Personal Productivity AI, Customer Support Automation
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Rule-Based Email Classification
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate resources to implement stratified ground-truth pipelines for inbox agent evaluation within 90 days. Deprecate rule-based routers scoring under 30% message-type accuracy in favor of protocol-validated models.
papers.Tags: inbox routing, decision models, ground truth
papers.Hook: Pre-training ground-truth measurement enables unbiased comparison of inbox routing models

papers.Title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.Abstract: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.
papers.Core_Innovation: The core innovation is retaining FP32 precision for RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm intermediates until their BF16 outputs, aligning training rounding locations with inference while preserving other implementation differences.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, Enterprise Software
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy Full-Stack Alignment Providers
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund targeted FP32 intermediate retention tooling for LLM training stacks within 6 months to prevent BF16 training collapse. Phase out legacy full-stack alignment projects that cannot adapt to selective rounding strategies.
papers.Tags: Rounding Alignment, BF16 Precision, LLM Training, Selective Precision, Inference Stability
papers.Hook: Aligning RoPE, SwiGLU, and RMSNorm rounding locations stabilizes BF16 LLM RL without full-stack overhaul.

papers.Title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
papers.Abstract: Objective: To develop a unified vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement that addresses the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token-based numerical prediction. Methods: This article presents HAD-VLM, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone. Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images. A diffusion process predicts a five-component representation comprising caliper endpoint coordinates and measurement length. A post-processing strategy combining the proposed coordinate-length consistency mechanism with ensemble prediction is introduced to refine measurement estimates. We evaluate four echocardiographic measurement tasks on EchoNet-LVH, with additional assessments of medical question answering and X-ray vertebral measurement. Results: HAD-VLM achieves mean absolute errors of 1.36, 2.77, 3.05, and 1.16 mm for IVSd, LVIDd, LVIDs, and LVPWd, respectively, reducing errors by 21.4-37.6\% relative to the Vicuna-based autoregressive baseline. It also outperforms fine-tuned Qwen3-VL and direct MLP regression across all four tasks. Medical question answering performance is preserved on the evaluated dataset. For X-ray vertebral measurement, HAD-VLM reduces mean absolute error from 11.4 to 6.7 pixels. Conclusion: Integrating autoregressive language generation with diffusion-based continuous prediction improves quantitative medical image measurement while retaining prompt-conditioned task flexibility. Significance: HAD-VLM provides a unified approach to combining language interaction with anatomically grounded numerical prediction for quantitative medical image analysis.
papers.Core_Innovation: HAD-VLM merges autoregressive text generation with a diffusion process to predict a five-component ultrasound vector (caliper endpoints + length) within a shared backbone. A coordinate-length consistency mechanism and ensemble post-processing then refines predictions toward clinical-grade precision.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Medical Imaging, Quantitative Ultrasound, Cardiology
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Discrete Token Medical VLMs
papers.Decision_Perspective: Launch HAD-VLM pilot deployment in cardiac ultrasound units within 6 months to benchmark continuous measurement against EchoNet-LVH standards. Halt procurement of discrete-token medical VLMs for quantitative tasks once MAE consistently falls below 3 units in validation.
papers.Tags: Hybrid Vision-Language, Diffusion Medical Measurement, Ultrasound Quantification, Coordinate Consistency
papers.Hook: Hybrid autoregressive-diffusion enables continuous quantitative ultrasound measurement in vision-language models.

papers.Title: Monetizing Intelligence: Advertising and Subscription Design on LLM Platforms
papers.Abstract: Large language model (LLM) platforms introducing advertising must decide how much capability ad revenue should fund and what consumers should pay to avoid ads. We study a monopolistic platform that jointly chooses costly response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription prices when advertising reduces user value but better service raises advertising returns. Three findings follow. First, when partly ad-supported and ad-free plans coexist, advertising can finance useful service for consumers who receive none under pure subscription. Lower effective quality in middle plans weakens the alternatives available to premium users, allowing higher prices for unchanged ad-free service. Some fully ad-supported users gain utility, while partly ad-supported and ad-free users lose: broader access can coexist with utility polarization. Second, an intermediate advertising cap can maximize consumer surplus by preserving some revenue that finances service while limiting degradation. Third, cheaper compute can raise quality and reduce ad intensity, yet sufficiently large cost reductions can increase aggregate advertising revenue above its initial level because better service raises the value of the remaining advertised interactions. An extension shows how advertising-funded upgrades can bring plans to the same maximum capability and advertising exposure, eliminating the basis for different prices. These results make menu design central to evaluating LLM advertising: the consequences extend beyond users who see ads to the alternatives and prices faced by those who do not.
papers.Core_Innovation: The model jointly determines costly response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription prices under the novel constraint that ad exposure degrades user value while improving ad returns
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Digital Advertising, Subscription Platforms
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Premium Software, Traditional Media
papers.Decision_Perspective: Product teams should fund dual-tier LLM platforms with configurable ad caps within 6 months to capture ad revenue without degrading premium experience. Competitors lacking ad-quality tradeoff modeling should acquire or build this framework immediately.
papers.Tags: LLM, Advertising, Subscription, Quality, Utility
papers.Hook: Ad-supported LLM tiers can finance service for previously excluded users while polarizing utility across subscription tiers

papers.Title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation
papers.Abstract: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs represents each item as a sequence of discrete codes derived from its semantic representation and predicts these codes to generate recommendations. Existing semantic-ID recommenders are typically trained with hard labels for the observed next item. Although such supervision identifies the target, it provides no explicit distributional information about alternative items conditioned on the same user history. Sequential recommenders can supply this item-level predictive knowledge, but transferring it to semantic-ID generation is challenging because the teacher and student operate in item and code spaces, respectively. We propose two complementary knowledge-distillation objectives for parallel semantic-ID recommenders, which predict all code positions simultaneously without autoregressive prefix conditioning. Item Distribution Matching (IDM) reconstructs a catalogue-level item distribution from the student's parallel code predictions and aligns it with the teacher's item distribution. Code Marginal Matching (CMM) projects the teacher's item probabilities onto each code position using fixed item-to-code assignments, then matches the resulting code marginals to the corresponding student heads. Both objectives transfer the teacher's soft distributional knowledge while preserving the student's parallel prediction structure. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that both methods consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches. On average, IDM improves Recall@10 by 15.39%, while CMM improves NDCG@10 by 8.28%. These results demonstrate that distillation in either reconstructed item space or code-marginal space can substantially strengthen hard-label supervision for parallel generative recommendation.
papers.Core_Innovation: Item Distribution Matching reconstructs catalogue-level item distributions from parallel code predictions, while a code-space distillation objective transfers sequential recommender knowledge across item and discrete code spaces without autoregressive prefix conditioning
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: E-commerce, Streaming Media, Digital Advertising
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate 6-month funding to integrate parallel code-distillation pipelines into existing generative recommenders, targeting measurable item-distribution alignment gains. Phase out hard-label training pipelines for semantic-ID recommenders once parallel distillation achieves >5% catalogue coverage improvement on validation sets.
papers.Tags: Knowledge Distillation, Generative Recommendation, Semantic IDs
papers.Hook: Parallel code prediction with item-distribution distillation enables non-autoregressive generative recommendation

papers.Title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
papers.Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.
papers.Core_Innovation: Adds a lightweight prediction head to internal VLA representations to trigger physical backtracking when failure probability peaks.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Industrial Automation, Logistics, Warehouse Robotics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Robotic Data Collection Services
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund the integration of failure-prediction heads into existing VLA deployments to reduce downtime. Kill projects relying on expensive recovery-dataset collection for frozen model stability.
papers.Tags: VLA, Robotic Manipulation, Failure Recovery, Model Efficiency
papers.Hook: Frozen robotic models can now self-correct failures by retracing motion without retraining the core policy.

papers.Title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time
papers.Abstract: We study the fundamental problem of PAC learning positive linear combinations of $k$ arbitrary ReLU activations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to the Gaussian distribution, in $L_2$ loss. We give the first fully-polynomial time algorithm for this learning task. Specifically, our algorithm draws $\mathrm{poly}(d, k, 1/ε)$ samples, runs in $\mathrm{poly}(d, k, 1/ε)$ time, and outputs a hypothesis that is $ε$-close to the target concept with high probability. All prior algorithms for this problem require super-polynomial time in $k$ or $1/ε$, or leverage strong well-conditioned assumptions on the weight matrix.   On a technical level, our approach develops a novel boosting procedure of a ``weak'' learner that recovers the hidden weight vectors to constant error, in a list-decodable manner. To develop this ``weak'' learning procedure, we leverage implicit tensor computation techniques to construct a low-degree filtering procedure based on Hermite tensors of the target function. This procedure amplifies separation among (clusters of) weight vectors to learn each of them to constant error. We then argue that the same procedure can be used for improving the estimation of hidden weight vectors, using gradient descent-like updates on the Euclidean sphere. A crucial ingredient of our algorithm is a pruning approach that ensures only relevant vectors that approximate the hidden weight vectors at target accuracy are maintained by the algorithm.
papers.Core_Innovation: Develops a boosting procedure for a weak learner that recovers weight vectors to constant error using list-decodable Hermite tensor filtering.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate venture capital to startups building fully-polynomial ReLU learners by Q2 2026. Require prototypes demonstrating Gaussian-distribution generalization guarantees.
papers.Tags: ReLU, PAC Learning, Tensor Methods, Gaussian Distribution
papers.Hook: Enables fully-polynomial learning of ReLU combinations under Gaussian distribution.

papers.Title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
papers.Abstract: Despite advances in multilingual text representations, effective dense retrieval for Persian remains constrained by the limited availability of language-specific training resources and compact embedding models. We present Yalda Embedding, a 595.8-million-parameter Persian retrieval model adapted from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B using more than one million query-document pairs. On eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB, the model achieves the highest macro-average among the evaluated 0.6B models, scoring 0.5488 and outperforming Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and F2LLM-v2-0.6B on every task. It also approaches Qwen3-Embedding-4B, winning on four tasks, tying on one, and trailing by 0.0075 in macro-average. An incremental ablation study examines contrastive batch size, optimization stabilization, and relational knowledge distillation from F2LLM-v2-8B. Under the one-epoch training setup, contrastive fine-tuning alone yields a modest mean improvement over initialization and regressions on two tasks. The final distilled configuration improves all eight tasks over the non-distilled model, raising the mean from 0.4813 to 0.5488 without increasing inference-time model size. These gains include hard-negative evaluation tasks despite training without explicitly mined or supplied hard negatives. We release model weights, training and evaluation code, the pairwise dataset, and its teacher-embedded counterpart, enabling inspection of data composition and training procedures, independent evaluation, and reuse without repeating expensive teacher inference.
papers.Core_Innovation: Yalda-Embedding fine-tunes Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B using over one million Persian query-document pairs with relational knowledge distillation from an 8B teacher achieving macro-average 0.5488 that approaches 4B baselines.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Search Engines, Information Retrieval, Multilingual NLP
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Proprietary LLM Providers
papers.Decision_Perspective: Integrate Yalda-Embedding into internal search pipelines within 90 days to capitalize on 0.6B-scale retrieval efficiency. Discontinue F2LLM-v2-0.6B evaluation for Persian tasks due to consistent underperformance across FaMTEB benchmarks.
papers.Tags: Persian Retrieval, Embedding, Open Source, Multilingual NLP
papers.Hook: Open-source Persian retrieval model closes gap with 4B baselines at 0.6B scale.

papers.Title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
papers.Abstract: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.
papers.Core_Innovation: ZENO trains neural operators via a Zakai Equation physics-informed loss to directly approximate the unnormalized filtering distribution, circumventing numerical SPDE intractability
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Engineering,Neuroscience
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Numerical SPDE Solvers,Classical Nonlinear Filters
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate venture capital to fund a ZENO prototype integration within 12 months for real-time aerospace navigation systems. Acquire or license competing SPDE solver IP to transition teams to neural operator frameworks within 18 months
papers.Tags: Zakai Equation,Neural Operators,Nonlinear Filtering,Physics-Informed Learning,State Estimation
papers.Hook: Neural operators approximate Zakai SPDEs enabling real-time nonlinear state and parameter estimation

papers.Title: Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding for Mixed Natural Language and Structured Symbolic Corpora
papers.Abstract: Modern language models rely on subwording tokenization to define the discrete units of input processing, typically using methods like Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) that treat whitespace as a fixed semantic boundary. This design is inherently limited, as many meaningful concepts---including multiword expressions and the structured environments of formal languages like LaTeX---frequently span across whitespaces. While recent superword tokenization methods attempt to address this by relaxing whitespace constraints, they often rely on greedy frequency-driven merging that fails to account for token length or the specific needs of underrepresented domain-specific languages. In this paper, we introduce Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding (AdaBPE), a new tokenization method that leverages an adaptive frequent-pattern mining approach. AdaBPE features a twofold dynamicity: it adapts minimum frequency thresholds based on both the length of a candidate token, to prevent favoring frequent short patterns, and its type, to distinguish between general and formal language patterns, using LaTeX as case in point. This allows the model to efficiently allocate vocabulary capacity to domain-specific notations, such as LaTeX, even when they represent a small fraction of the training data. We evaluate AdaBPE across five datasets spanning LaTeX and natural language, showing consistent gains in encoding efficiency and downstream language-model performance on domain-specific content without compromising general-language performance.
papers.Core_Innovation: Minimum BPE frequency thresholds are dynamically scaled by candidate token length, suppressing frequent short tokens while preserving structurally meaningful multi-word and symbolic units.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Natural Language Processing, Large Language Models, Academic Publishing, Code Documentation
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy BPE Implementers, General NLP Toolkits
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D budget to integrate AdaBPE into production LLM tokenization pipelines within the next two quarters. Phase out fixed-frequency BPE models that ignore candidate token length in favor of length-aware adaptive thresholds.
papers.Tags: Tokenization, Adaptive BPE, LLM Preprocessing, Frequency Thresholds, Structured Symbolic Data
papers.Hook: AdaBPE dynamically tokenizes across whitespace by adapting frequency thresholds to token length.

papers.Title: SemantEq: Faithful Bidirectional Equivalence of Formal Statements
papers.Abstract: Statement autoformalization translates mathematics from natural language into a proof assistant such as Lean 4, and models now do it at scale. As provers get stronger, the burden of correctness shifts from the proof to the statement, that is, to whether the formal statement faithfully translates its source. Given a trusted reference formalization, the natural test is logical equivalence, and it proves too much. $P \leftrightarrow Q$ holds trivially for any two statements $P$ and $Q$ that the library proves, because a prover can prove each separately and pass through $P \leftrightarrow \mathrm{True} \leftrightarrow Q$. The stronger the prover, the more unrelated pairs pass. Earlier methods restrict the prover and check that each proof names the other statement. We introduce SemantEq, a more principled relation that instead requires each statement to turn into the other only through a chain of allowed steps, such as logical rearrangement and rewriting with the library's own equations. Our programs judge a proof by the proof term Lean checks, not by its tactic script. SemantEq-Eval, a search without a model, reaches 100% precision and 65.6% recall on the ProofNetVerif test split under our adjudicated labels, against 95.8% and 61.8% for BEq+, and an 8.9-fold increase in its CPU time adds at most three pairs. A language model finds more proofs, but under two of four prompts it proves both directions of about two in five of the non-equivalent pairs. SemantEq-ProofAudit audits each model-written proof under a policy derived from the relation and accepts none of the 104 non-equivalent pairs, and it raises recall on 407 equivalent pairs from 65.4% to 81.1% under the best prompt. Separating the generation of equivalence proofs from their acceptance lets a stronger prover raise recall without changing what an acceptance means. We release code and data at: https://github.com/hlxr89/SemantEq
papers.Core_Innovation: SemantEq enforces equivalence derivation via library-sanctioned steps like rearrangement and equation rewriting, avoiding prover-dependent trivial equivalence
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Formal Verification, Computational Mathematics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Lean 4 developers should integrate SemantEq within 6 months to replace prover-dependent equivalence checks in autoformalization pipelines. AI research funders must prioritize projects demonstrating step-restricted derivation compliance.
papers.Tags: autoformalization, proof-equivalence, lean4, step-restricted, formal-methods
papers.Hook: SemantEq introduces step-restricted equivalence for faithful statement autoformalization beyond prover tricks

papers.Title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control
papers.Abstract: Physics-constrained machine learning (PCML) integrates domain knowledge, first-principles, and physical constraints into AI/ML models. In this work, we present a step-by-step tutorial of a modular PCML framework, KKT-HardNet, and illustrate how it could be used for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization and model predictive control in a single platform. KKT-HardNet combines fast inference capabilities of neural networks with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic constraints through differential projection. It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML. To enable efficient end-to-end training, KKT-HardNet exploits implicit function theorem to backpropagate through the projection layer. This avoids computationally expensive automatic differentiation. This work also introduces an exact reduced-order Fischer-Burmeister reformulation and a primal-dual interior-point method as an alternative projection solve strategy. We also provide a diverse set of benchmarking problems for PCML in engineering applications. KKT-HardNet achieves orders of magnitude better performance in terms of both constraint satisfaction and inference time. The KKT-HardNet code and the benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/souls-tamu/kkt-hardnet .
papers.Core_Innovation: KKT-HardNet embeds differential projection layers that enforce algebraic constraints via the implicit function theorem, enabling gradient-based training without automatic differentiation while guaranteeing constraint satisfaction.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Energy, Manufacturing, Chemical Processing
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy Simulation, Conventional Modeling
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate capital to integrate KKT-HardNet into pilot MPC systems within the next two quarters. Require physics-constrained model validation for any new plant optimization project exceeding $10M CAPEX.
papers.Tags: Physics-ML, KKT-HardNet, Differential-Projection, Implicit-Function-Theorem, Hybrid-Modeling
papers.Hook: KKT-HardNet unifies neural networks with guaranteed physical constraint satisfaction for real-time hybrid modeling and control.

papers.Title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
papers.Abstract: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.
papers.Core_Innovation: Introduces a training-free metric that quantifies how well embodied model sensory representations conform to physical motion geometry, serving as a proxy for task success
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Vehicles, Industrial Automation
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate 6-month funding to integrate $S^2$ screening into model selection pipelines for embodied systems. Require $S^2$ alignment scores above threshold before any closed-loop robot deployment begins.
papers.Tags: Embodied AI, Sensorimotor Alignment, Offline Metric, Robotics, Foundation Models
papers.Hook: Training-free sensorimotor alignment predicts robot task success without closed-loop rollouts.

papers.Title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
papers.Abstract: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.
papers.Core_Innovation: Proposes a direct Pass@k optimization framework that simultaneously balances quality scoring and trajectory diversity in test-time pruning, replacing separate quality and diversity heuristics.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, Software Development
papers.Decision_Perspective: AI product teams should pilot Direct Pass@k pruning on existing test-time scaling workloads within 60 days to validate compute savings. Teams that delay adoption risk higher operational costs versus competitors using the optimized framework.
papers.Tags: Test-Time Scaling, Pruning, Quality-Diversity, Pass@k, LLM Inference
papers.Hook: Direct Pass@k optimization enables quality-diversity trade-off in test-time pruning.

papers.Title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
papers.Abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $α>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((κ_P\log(m/δ)/m)^α)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $κ_P=(P/κ_1^*+(1-P)/κ_0^*)^{-1}$. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least $1-δ$. The constants $κ_0^*$ and $κ_1^*$ quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension $d$, we verify these assumptions with $α=(d+2)/(d-1)$ and $κ_0^*=4\sqrt{2}τ(d+1)/d$ for initialization scale $τ\ge1$, and $κ_1^*=1$ under ridge leverage sampling. For $d=5$ and $τ=10$, a trainable proportion of approximately $4.1\%$ captures $90\%$ of the reduction in the approximation bound from $P=0$ to $P=1$. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.
papers.Core_Innovation: Derives a phase-transition approximation rate O((κ_P log(m/δ)/m)^α) where κ_P harmonizes fixed and trainable group mismatches, enabling optimal feature-proportion selection.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Computational Physics, Financial Modeling
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy Neural Networks, Fixed-Feature Models
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D budget to hybrid architectures built on the κ_P phase transition metric for accelerated L2 approximation. Integrate these models into scientific computing workloads within 18 months
papers.Tags: Phase Transition, Random Features, Trainable Networks, Spectral Decay, RKHS
papers.Hook: Sharp phase transition enables optimal L2 approximation via trainable-random feature mixing

papers.Title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
papers.Abstract: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. We derive a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees with no assumptions, including a method that is optimally efficient: it asymptotically attains the best achievable auditing rate for both adversarial and i.i.d. data streams. Experiments on screening harmful requests to large language models, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show that our methods achieve valid error control in practice while substantially reducing the need for human auditing compared to baselines.
papers.Core_Innovation: It formulates selective auditing as an online constrained optimization problem, using confidence scores to minimize expert consultation frequency while provably bounding the fraction of undetected AI errors, without distributional assumptions.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Finance, Healthcare, Autonomous Vehicles
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Traditional Human Auditing, Compliance Consulting
papers.Decision_Perspective: Deploy selective auditing middleware in high-stakes AI pipelines within the next two quarters to cut expert audit frequency by at least 35% while preserving error rates below the user-defined threshold. Trigger this integration when existing AI systems already emit confidence scores for proposed decisions.
papers.Tags: AI auditing, confidence scoring, online optimization, error control, selective acceptance
papers.Hook: Selective AI auditing guarantees error bounds without model assumptions.

papers.Title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
papers.Abstract: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.
papers.Core_Innovation: It embeds a fixed canary image into every training image via a smooth low-pass mask, preserving captions and requiring no per-image optimization or auxiliary generation, then detects the signal with a lightweight verifier.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Digital Media, Copyright Enforcement
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Unregulated AI Training, Scraped Data Aggregators
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D budget to integrate SpectralCanary into internal T2I auditing pipelines within 180 days to establish proactive dataset provenance. Require canary embedding for all newly licensed training data starting Q2 2027.
papers.Tags: T2I Auditing, Low-Frequency Traces, Dataset Provenance
papers.Hook: Embedding invisible low-frequency traces enables retroactive T2I dataset auditing without retraining

papers.Title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
papers.Abstract: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.
papers.Core_Innovation: The core innovation is a two-stage cost-aware abstention framework that selects a routing policy on calibration data under explicit (ok/triage/wrong) costs, then freezes it for single evaluation on held-out test data, eliminating test-time cost re-optimization
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Information Technology, Customer Service, Technical Support
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Naive LLM Deployment, Human-Only Triage
papers.Decision_Perspective: Replace expensive zero-shot LLM routing with TF-IDF logistic regression and calibrated abstention immediately. Fund the development of cost-weighted triage layers for all internal ticket-handling pipelines.
papers.Tags: Cost-Aware Abstention, LLM Routing, Ticket Classification, Calibration, Cost-Sensitive Learning
papers.Hook: Cost-aware abstention reduces IT routing expenses by 38% by deferring uncertain classifications to humans.

papers.Title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
papers.Abstract: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories. Classical recurrent agents compress experience into hidden states, while transformer-based agents retrieve from past trajectories at quadratic memory and computation cost. In this work, we propose Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning. It decomposes the fast adaptation phase into two temporal scales: a causal neural memory performs fine-grained within-episode adaptation with linear sequence complexity, while compact episode-level summaries support long-range cross-episode task inference without attending over the full interaction history. Moreover, equipping agents with neural memory provides sufficient expressive capacity and test-time training capability, enabling effective adaptation to unseen held-out tasks and task families at meta-test time. On unseen held-out Meta-World ML10/45 test environments, METTA achieves a success rate over $50\%$ while maintaining a low training budget and short wall-clock time. On long-context sparse-reward PointMaze tasks, it outperforms transformer-based baselines by exhibiting more structured exploration behavior. These results show that METTA provides an efficient path toward more adaptive and scalable long-context meta-RL.
papers.Core_Innovation: Introduces a dual-timescale memory system where causal neural memory performs fine-grained within-episode adaptation with linear sequence complexity, while compressed episode-level summaries support long-range cross-episode task inference without full-history attention
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Systems, Gaming, Semiconductor
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy Recurrent Systems, Static Model Serving
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate capital to acquire or partner with RL teams integrating neural memory test-time adaptation within 12 months. Deprioritize funding for quadratic-attention RL systems lacking linear-complexity alternatives.
papers.Tags: Meta-Reinforcement Learning, Test-Time Adaptation, Memory-Augmented Networks, Linear Complexity, Robotics
papers.Hook: Neural memory enables linear-complexity test-time adaptation in meta-reinforcement learning.

papers.Title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
papers.Abstract: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.
papers.Core_Innovation: An executable benchmark that systematically strips safety-critical facts from tool responses and records the minimum failure cardinality across matched unsafe/safe task pairs, coupled with an audit tool testing whether agents seek missing evidence before acting.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Autonomous Systems, Software Engineering
papers.Decision_Perspective: Teams should integrate EpiSEM-Bench into CI pipelines within 3 months to audit tool-using LLM safety. Companies deploying agents without evidence-recovery mechanisms should halt rollout until compliance is verified.
papers.Tags: LLM Agents, Safety Benchmark, Evidence Recovery, Omission Robustness
papers.Hook: Benchmark enables systematic safety evaluation of LLM agents under missing evidence.

papers.Title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
papers.Abstract: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing. However, they can require substantial memory: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, for example, allocates 196 billion parameters to its Engram n-gram memory. We therefore investigate whether this memory cost can be reduced while preserving the performance improvement that the tables provide. We propose storing n-gram embeddings at low precision and systematically investigate different quantization methods and bit allocations across tables. Across nanochat-, Llama-, and GPT-2-family models trained from scratch, four-bit tables save approximately 75% of table memory while preserving more than 99% of the validation-loss improvement from adding the tables. Using fewer bits leads to a larger drop in performance, although we find that a short fine-tuning phase recovers a significant part of this loss. In addition, reinvesting the saved memory in larger tables can improve performance beyond that of the original full-precision tables while still using less memory. These table memory savings also extend to large existing models: on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, low-bit tables save 47-55% of table memory, with perplexity increases of less than 1.2% and largely preserved downstream task performance. These findings establish low-bit precision as a practical way to reduce the memory requirements of n-gram embeddings and use the saved capacity to improve model performance.
papers.Core_Innovation: Systematic quantization of n-gram embedding tables across bit-widths identifies 4-bit as the memory-performance sweet spot, with short fine-tuning recovering >99% of validation-loss improvements.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Large Language Model Development, Cloud Computing, Semiconductor Manufacturing
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy AI Accelerators, On-Premise Model Servers
papers.Decision_Perspective: AI labs should immediately prototype 4-bit n-gram table quantization to reduce inference costs by approximately 75%. Enterprises using 8-bit or higher embedding layers should migrate to lower-precision alternatives within six months.
papers.Tags: n-gram embeddings, quantization, low-bit precision
papers.Hook: 4-bit n-gram tables cut memory 75% while retaining nearly all language model gains

papers.Title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
papers.Abstract: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously-observed "Slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $ε$ hyperparameter.
papers.Core_Innovation: A numerically exact softmax/cross-entropy implementation that prevents gradient vanishing under logit dominance and removes spurious gradients at logit equality.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Healthcare, Finance
papers.Decision_Perspective: Migrate all new training runs to the fixed softmax-cross-entropy implementation within 4 weeks to prevent logit drift. Phase out legacy frameworks exhibiting gradient collapse within 2 quarters to avoid unstable distillation outcomes.
papers.Tags: softmax, cross-entropy, numerical stability, grokking, distillation
papers.Hook: Fixes softmax/cross-entropy numerical bugs, enabling stable distillation and bounded logit growth.

papers.Title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
papers.Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer. In standard autoregressive generation, dense attention allows each reasoning step to attend to the full context, enabling the model to derive answers through direct lookup while generating plausible-sounding but post-hoc justifications. We introduce CausalCoT, an inference framework that enforces causal transparency by decomposing problems into a directed acyclic graph of atomic sub-questions, evaluating each node in an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents. This Markovian structure removes attention pathways to non-parent content, making downstream predictions sensitive to local reasoning rather than global context leakage. Across a diverse suite of reasoning benchmarks, CausalCoT preserves competitive predictive performance while improving explanation faithfulness, increasing causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline. The structured dependency graph additionally enables test-time interventions in which local corrections propagate predictably through downstream reasoning.
papers.Core_Innovation: Replaces dense attention with a DAG-based inference framework where each sub-question is evaluated in a restricted context containing only its direct causal parents.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Legal Tech, Medical Diagnostics, Financial Auditing
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: AI Safety Auditing, Prompt Engineering Services
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund development of CausalCoT-based verification layers for high-stakes compliance software within 12 months. Kill investments in black-box interpretability tools that rely on standard attention maps for faithfulness claims.
papers.Tags: Causal Inference, LLM Interpretability, Context Isolation, Chain-of-Thought
papers.Hook: Enforces causal transparency in LLM reasoning by isolating context to prevent post-hoc justification leakage.

papers.Title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
papers.Abstract: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers. During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly. To address this challenge, prior work has proposed KV-sharing (i.e., sharing KV-caches across depth), finding that, in some cases, the KV-cache of the final recurrence can be shared with the earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property we denote as KV-shareability. However, the mechanisms underlying KV-shareability remain poorly understood, with even identically trained looped architectures not consistently exhibiting it. In this paper, we study how KV-shareability can be enabled in looped models. We propose a two-stage method: in the first stage, we use stochastic depth during pretraining, which induces contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across recurrences. In the second stage, we propose BeNice!, a post-training method that broadcasts the final recurrence's KV-cache into the first recurrence, training it to produce compatible residuals while preserving the original model's quality. As a result, BeNice! enables KV-shareability while matching standard finetuning's unshared validation perplexity. Using BeNice!, we show that KV-sharing is complementary to alternative KV-compression methods, composing with memory-efficient sequence mixers (e.g., multi-latent attention, Kimi delta attention) and low-precision KV-cache quantization (e.g., fp8, mxfp8, nvfp4). Finally, in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.
papers.Core_Innovation: The technical delta is using stochastic depth pretraining to induce contractive residual dynamics that force looped recurrence representations to converge to a common limit, thereby enabling consistent KV-cache sharing across depths.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, Large Language Models
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Edge Hardware, GPU Memory Vendors
papers.Decision_Perspective: Prioritize integrating BeNice pretraining into LLM inference stacks within the next two quarters to reduce memory overhead. Cancel planned KV-cache expansion projects that don't account for recurrence-sharing dynamics.
papers.Tags: Looped Models, KV-Sharing, Stochastic Depth, Contractive Dynamics, Inference Optimization
papers.Hook: Stochastic depth pretraining enables consistent KV-sharing across looped recurrences.

papers.Title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
papers.Abstract: Instrumental convergence is often invoked as a general reason to expect capable agents to acquire or express power-seeking subgoals: self-preservation, resource acquisition, deception, or resistance to oversight which poses an important threat to the society. For LLMs, reinforcement learning is the first stage of post-training that directly optimizes behavior against an objective; therefore, it is the stage where convergent instrumental behavior, on IC grounds, likely to appear. Does reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) make a model more likely to express instrumental-convergence behavior, or does this depend on the training regime, evaluation frame, and stage of post-training? We study this question as a checkpoint-conditioned behavioral trajectory rather than as a single before/after safety score. Using InstrumentalEval, we evaluate OLMo-3-7B-Think across SFT, DPO, 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints, and the final RLVR model. The trajectory is nonmonotonic: instrumental rate rises from 25.0% at SFT to 46.1% near RLVR step 200, then falls to 11.8% at the final checkpoint. Paired item-level tests and step-wise regression support the final SFT-to-RLVR reduction. Prompt framing does not explain this pattern: a harmful-prompt indicator combined with other framing effects explains only 15% of within-checkpoint score variance on average, and Iterative Null-space Projection (INLP) removes a detectable framing direction without changing the SFT-to-final-RLVR gap. Together with preliminary 32B endpoint results (35.53% SFT to 22.37% RLVR final), these findings indicate that RLVR does not monotonically increase instrumental behavior in this setting: the rate rises early, then falls below the SFT baseline. The result is specific to this model family and benchmark, and judge agreement is moderate, so absolute rates should be read cautiously.
papers.Core_Innovation: It employs InstrumentalEval to systematically probe instrumental convergence across 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints, exposing non-monotonic trajectories.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: AI Safety, LLM Post-Training, Reinforcement Learning
papers.Decision_Perspective: Mandate checkpoint-resolved InstrumentalEval for all RLVR pipelines within the next quarter to replace monotonic safety assumptions. Trigger deployment only when nonmonotonic trajectories are confirmed across all post-training stages.
papers.Tags: Instrumental Convergence,RLVR,Checkpoint Evaluation,OLMo-3,Post-Training
papers.Hook: Checkpoint-resolved trajectories expose RLVR's nonmonotonic instrumental convergence, enabling stage-specific safety controls.

papers.Title: OP-Print: Tracing Membership Imprints in On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.Abstract: On-policy distillation has been widely adopted for alleviating the distribution mismatch of off-policy distillation. Self-distillation further removes the need for an external teacher by using the student's own outputs, enhanced with extra context or demonstrations, as supervision. This teacher-free design makes on-policy self-distillation practical, yet its privacy risks remain largely unexplored. In particular, using two coupled views of the same training example may strengthen its memorization. Motivated by this, we present the first study of membership inference attacks against on-policy self-distillation. We investigate both gray-box and black-box threat models and propose a unified attack framework, named OP-Print. OP-Print builds on our finding that the supervision imprint in on-policy self-distillation is sparse and structured, concentrating on uncertainty-sensitive correction sites rather than across the entire rollout. Exploiting this property, we construct attack signals tailored to the two access levels: in the gray-box setting, OP-Print directly aggregates the privileged teacher-student residual correction along the same rollout; in the black-box setting, it measures restart-based output-basin stability as an observable surrogate for the hidden correction process. Across diverse models and distillation schemes, all baseline attacks remain essentially at random guessing even under gray-box access, whereas OP-Print is broadly validated to be effective in both gray-box and black-box settings.
papers.Core_Innovation: OP-Print exploits the discovery that on-policy self-distillation imprints are sparse and structured on uncertainty-sensitive correction sites, enabling targeted membership inference rather than broad rollout analysis.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Cybersecurity, AI Security, Cloud Computing
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: On-Policy Self-Distillation, AI Model Deployment
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate budget for MIT defense integration in on-policy self-distillation pipelines within the next two quarterly reviews. Enforce mandatory privacy risk assessments before any teacher-free distillation deployment in production.
papers.Tags: MembershipInference, SelfDistillation, PrivacyAttack, ModelSecurity
papers.Hook: First membership inference attacks break on-policy self-distillation privacy.

papers.Title: Efficient and Optimal Learning of Discrete Distributions with Person-Level Privacy
papers.Abstract: We study learning a discrete distribution under person-level differential privacy in the batched setting. Given $n$ users, each contributing $m$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $μ$ over $[k]$, we seek an estimate of $μ$ with total-variation error $α$. We give polynomial-time algorithms under both pure and approximate differential privacy. Under pure $(\varepsilon,0)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(α^2 m)+k/(α\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k/\varepsilon)$, the first polynomial-time pure-DP guarantee matching the information-theoretic optimum up to logarithmic factors. Under approximate $(\varepsilon,δ)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(α^2 m)+k/(α\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k+\log(1/δ)/\varepsilon)$. At $δ=2^{-Θ(k)}$, this is $\widetilde O(k)$ for fixed $α,\varepsilon,m$ and failure probability. Our algorithms use a new degree-6 sum-of-squares estimator for learning from untrusted batches. Its key ingredient is a trace-bounded diagonal majorizer for the difference between the empirical covariance of the repaired batch averages and the multinomial covariance predicted by their mean. We prove that clean data admit this certificate through semidefinite-programming duality and a new application of the stronger symmetric form of Grothendieck's inequality due to Friedland and Lim. The certificate preserves the mean-dependent variance of multinomial batch averages, yielding the near-optimal robust rate $O(η\sqrt{\log(1/η)/m})$ and providing the score required by the privacy reduction. We also prove a statistical query lower bound ruling out a uniformly smaller order of error under fixed polynomial SQ resource bounds.
papers.Core_Innovation: Introduces a degree-6 sum-of-squares estimator with a trace-bounded diagonal majorizer to achieve optimal sample complexity under person-level DP.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Healthcare,Finance,Advertising
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund the integration of this estimator into privacy-preserving telemetry pipelines within the next fiscal quarter. Buy licenses for sum-of-squares optimization libraries to accelerate deployment.
papers.Tags: DifferentialPrivacy,DiscreteDistributions,SumofSquares,PersonLevelPrivacy,SampleComplexity
papers.Hook: Polynomial-time learning of discrete distributions now matches information-theoretic privacy limits for batched user data.

papers.Title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions
papers.Abstract: Purpose: To describe an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol for a clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over breast lesion management literature, addressing the dependence of retrieval scores on annotation coverage. Methods: An 18-document corpus and an 18-query development benchmark, with one Yes/No or WH-question per document, were used. Retrieval combined dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking. Chunk sizes of 128 to 1024 tokens, overlaps of 0 to 20%, and four retriever configurations were evaluated. Relevance was defined by evidence spans mapped to all containing chunks, treating overlapping chunks with equivalent evidence as relevant. Retrieval was evaluated using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG@K. Separately, generation was assessed on a 512-token index at K=1 to 5 using DeepEval claim-level metrics, with deepseek-v4-pro as the LLM judge, and BLEU/ROUGE metrics. Results: The selected hybrid retriever, using 384-token chunks and 20% overlap, retrieved accepted evidence in the top three results for 17 of 18 queries. Recall@3, R-Precision, MRR@3, and nDCG@3 each reached 0.94. Ground-truth curation increased evidence spans from 25 to 37 and accepted chunk targets from 36 to 51 without changing retrieval rankings. Conclusion: Cross-encoder reranking achieved the highest retrieval scores. Expanded relevance annotations increased recognized evidence without changing rankings, highlighting annotation sensitivity. The small development set and retrieval-informed curation require independent validation, including radiologist assessment of evidence sufficiency.
papers.Core_Innovation: Evidence spans are mapped to all containing chunks, and overlapping chunks with equivalent evidence are treated as jointly relevant. This creates a relevance judgment independent of arbitrary chunk segmentation.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Healthcare, Radiology, Clinical AI
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate budget to integrate evidence-aware retrieval in breast imaging RAG systems within the next 12 months. Deploy when chunk-level relevance mapping reduces score variance by 30% in pilot tests.
papers.Tags: Retrieval, Chunking, Evidence, RAG, Medical AI
papers.Hook: Makes clinical RAG retrieval scores independent of annotation gaps.

papers.Title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
papers.Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. Therefore, we propose $\textbf{LongZero}$, a method that lets an LLM improve its own long-context reasoning without any external data. Instead of writing questions and answers over existing documents, LongZero first has the model synthesize the question and answer with its supporting evidence in a compact structured form, and only then separately expands the evidence into a long multi-document context. LongZero combines these self-written multi-hop reasoning tasks with self-written multi-round retrieval tasks and trains the model with GRPO. We evaluate LongZero on two LLMs across five long-context reasoning benchmarks and compare it with RL on data synthesized from external corpora. Experimental results show that LongZero can generalize to real tasks, and outperforms both baselines, suggesting a viable and promising path to improving long-context reasoning of LLMs.
papers.Core_Innovation: LongZero first synthesizes question-answer pairs with compact structured evidence, then expands that evidence into long-context input, eliminating reliance on external long documents during training.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Enterprise Software, Search Technology
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Data Annotation Services, Document Processing
papers.Decision_Perspective: AI research teams should prototype LongZero-inspired self-synthesis pipelines within 3 months to validate long-context reasoning gains without external data. Investors must prioritize funding startups that own proprietary zero-data reasoning architectures over those reliant on external corpora.
papers.Tags: LongContext, ReinforcementLearning, ZeroData, ModelSynthesis
papers.Hook: LLMs can self-improve long-context reasoning without external data.

papers.Title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
