papers.Abstract: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outranks the fixed one, indicating that existing uniform computation both wastes capacity on already-converged items and sacrifices overall recommendation quality. These observations motivate a shift from fixed-depth computation to item-level adaptive reasoning. To this end, we propose LoopRec. LoopRec recursively applies a single weight-shared block and introduces a lightweight gate at each recursion boundary that makes a binary exit-or-continue decision for every item independently. Items whose representations have sufficiently matured exit early, while those requiring deeper reasoning continue to subsequent recursions. This design converts the fixed global depth into a learned, per-item property without auxiliary depth labels, and is readily adaptable to diverse backbone architectures. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks with four backbone families demonstrate that LoopRec consistently outperforms matched fixed-depth counterparts. Further analysis reveals that LoopRec's learned allocation exhibits interpretable patterns aligned with our post-hoc oracle analysis: lower-frequency items and more recent interactions naturally receive deeper computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Elpmis117/LoopRec.
papers.Core_Innovation: LoopRec replaces fixed-depth processing with a weight-shared recursive block and lightweight gating to adaptively halt computation per sequence item
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: E-commerce, Streaming Media, Digital Advertising
papers.Decision_Perspective: Prototype LoopRec's adaptive gating in our recommendation pipeline within Q1 2026 to replace fixed-depth processing. Deprecate static budget modules once per-item computation savings exceed 20% without quality degradation.
papers.Tags: Sequential Recommendation, Adaptive Computation, Recursive Networks, Item-level Gating, Recommendation Systems
papers.Hook: Dynamic per-item computation depth replaces fixed budgets in sequential recommendation

papers.Title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
papers.Abstract: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. Without calibrating these physics factors for world models, predictions tend to regress toward an empirical prior and induce severe drift in novel test scenes. To this end, we propose PhysiCalWorld, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling. Our method encodes an exploratory interaction clip collected within the test scene into a compact physics descriptor token, which grounds subsequent predictions in the scene's actual physical behavior. PhysiCalWorld is trained end-to-end with the latent prediction loss alone, without physics labels. At inference time, the descriptor token is extracted once and can be reused across rollouts with negligible compute overhead. We evaluate PhysiCalWorld across four environments covering diverse physics variations and show that it substantially improves rollout prediction accuracy and visual planning success rate. The learned descriptors also form a physically structured latent space and generalize beyond the physics ranges seen during training.
papers.Core_Innovation: A compact physics descriptor token, extracted from exploratory interaction clips, enables in-context calibration of action-conditioned world models trained purely on latent prediction loss, eliminating the need for fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Driving, Virtual Production, Manufacturing
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Fine-Tuned World Model Providers, Analytical Physics Modeling
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding to pilot in-context physics calibration in flagship autonomous driving simulators within the next 2 quarters. Phase out legacy fine-tuning pipelines for scene-specific physics adaptation once baseline performance is matched.
papers.Tags: world models, physics calibration, in-context learning, robotics simulation, descriptor token
papers.Hook: World models adapt instantly to real physics dynamics via in-context prompting, eliminating fine-tuning.

papers.Title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
papers.Abstract: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.
papers.Core_Innovation: The paper introduces a boosting argument that geometrically shrinks a search region, enabling epsilon-approximate fixed point computation for d-dimensional L_inf nonexpansive mappings in log(1/eps)^O(log^2 d) time.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Computational Finance, Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Exponential Solvers
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund integration of quasipolynomial L_inf solvers into commercial game theory platforms within 18 months. Acquire early-adopter licenses from leading research groups releasing open-source implementations.
papers.Tags: Quasipolynomial, Fixed-Point, ell_inf, Stochastic Games, Boosting
papers.Hook: New quasipolynomial algorithm computes epsilon-approximate L_inf fixed points in log(1/eps)^O(log^2 d) time.

papers.Title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
papers.Abstract: We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of interest. This is important for applications in machine learning: we prove generalization error bounds for classification with non-i.i.d., regenerative data. These bounds can be used to define learning objectives: by minimizing the first-order term only in the bound, we define agnostic classifiers that still satisfy oracle inequalities. We also show that the bound on the average deviation provided by our results is minimax-optimal in the sample size and in the expected regeneration time. Finally, we combine the Bernstein inequality with a regenerative strong approximation to obtain a Gaussian approximation using an observable block variance estimator.
papers.Core_Innovation: The paper introduces a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for regenerative processes that conditions on observed cycle lengths, retains explicit truncation and cycle-ending terms, and isolates a residual tail term involving regeneration time tails. This structural decomposition enables data-dependent generalization bounds for classification without i.i.d. assumptions.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Machine Learning, Finance, Healthcare
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Classical Statistics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate venture capital to startups building self-normalized inequality estimators for regenerative time-series within 18 months. Acquire or hire talent specializing in non-i.i.d. generalization theory to maintain competitive positioning.
papers.Tags: Self-normalized Bernstein, Regenerative Processes, Generalization Bounds, Non-i.i.d. Learning
papers.Hook: Self-normalized Bernstein inequality for regenerative processes enables generalization bounds for non-i.i.d. classification.

papers.Title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks
papers.Abstract: The success of convolutional neural networks is often attributed to locality and weight sharing. However, how these two properties separately shape learning, and how their effects depend on the spatial correlations of natural images, remain poorly understood. We address these questions in a teacher-student model with a convolutional teacher acting on $P$ input positions with correlation $c$ between positions. We compare convolutional and locally connected students trained by online stochastic gradient descent, and derive ordinary differential equations that describe their dynamics exactly in the limit of large feature dimension $D$. For uncorrelated positions ($c = 0$), the two students follow the same learning trajectory, with the convolutional student learning exactly $P$ times faster. We also find that locality affects the sample complexity: a student that matches the kernel size of the teacher recovers it from $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D)$ samples, whereas $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D\log(D))$ samples are needed with a larger kernel. For $c > 0$, spatial correlations can reduce the advantage of weight sharing. The asymptotic error of the convolutional student grows with $c$, whereas that of the locally connected student is independent of $c$ and overall lower when evaluated at the same learning rate. When the learning rate is instead tuned to the training horizon, however, the locally connected student wins at early times and the convolutional student at late times, with a transition that we predict analytically.
papers.Core_Innovation: Derivation of exact ordinary differential equations for convolutional student-teacher dynamics in the large-feature-dimension limit, proving that weight sharing yields a P-fold speed advantage only under uncorrelated inputs, while kernel-size-matched locality achieves optimal sample complexity O(D) versus O(D log D) for locally connected students
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Computer Vision, Autonomous Vehicles, Medical Imaging, Robotics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Traditional Convolutional Design, Manual Feature Extraction
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund the development of kernel-size-matched locally connected student architectures for uncorrelated image datasets within 18 months to capture the O(D) sample efficiency gain. Phase out legacy CNN pipelines that lack weight-sharing optimization as they fail the correlation-aware efficiency trigger.
papers.Tags: convolutional neural networks, teacher-student dynamics, sample complexity, weight sharing, locality
papers.Hook: Convolutional vs locally connected students follow learning paths when inputs are uncorrelated, revealing weight sharing's P-fold speed advantage

papers.Title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
papers.Abstract: Through a tangle of real-world interactions, from synthetic training pipelines to data shared on the open web, frontier LLMs absorb what their predecessors and competitors create. How well does each model play its role in this ecosystem, as a creator and as a solver? We introduce Environment Duels, a dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates both capabilities on interactive environments. Each model writes environments, each with a privileged hint, aiming for tasks that capable solvers fail without the hint and pass with it. Across nine frontier LLMs, solving and authoring prove to be distinct skills: the strongest solvers are not the strongest authors, while smaller models learn more from how others played and write the hardest environments and the most useful hints. Beyond the scores, the pairwise interactions form a microcosm of how models affect one another. Head-to-head outcomes are transitive and so yield a stable ranking; independent authors converge on the same designs; and in a reinforcement-learning study with Qwen3.8-27B, the learner's hint lift on an author's environments tracks how much training on those environments improves it on held-out reasoning and agentic benchmarks, whether the environments are its own or another model's. Each of these patterns has a counterpart in how models shape one another outside the duel. By staging these interactions under controlled conditions, Environment Duels offers a window onto how LLMs teach, challenge and learn from one another. Code is available at https://github.com/LLM-Duels/EnvDuels.
papers.Core_Innovation: The core innovation is an agentic benchmark where environment authors embed privileged hints to create tasks solvable only with hint assistance, thereby dissociating authoring from solving aptitude across models.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Educational Technology
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Static Benchmark Maintenance, Manual Curriculum Design
papers.Decision_Perspective: Build an internal Environment Duels framework within 3 months to quantify authoring-skill gaps in current LLM pipelines. Fund specialized author-model teams to generate high-hint-value environments before competitor releases.
papers.Tags: LLM Co-Evolution, Agentic Benchmark, Environment Design, Model Authoring, Solving Skill
papers.Hook: Enables first dynamic evaluation of LLM co-evolution via agentic environment duels.

papers.Title: The End of Consensus Research?
papers.Abstract: Consensus is a fundamental problem in distributed computing and at the core of state machine replication (SMR). Despite decades of active human research, discovering practical low-latency solutions to the problem is still open, as it requires combining protocol knowledge, correctness reasoning, implementation, and experimental evaluation. We report on how AI helped us discover A-greement, a new consensus protocol for geo-replicated state machines that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art solutions. Averaged across six deployments with 5 or 9 replicas, A-greement reduces the mean latency of a geo-distributed key-value store over the fastest baseline by 12.2% and 33.3% on write-heavy and read-heavy workloads, respectively, and matches the fastest baseline on read-only workloads. A-greement combines lease-authorized local reads, direct client learning for leader-ordered writes, and a fast fixed-quorum per-key write path, selected according to network topology and workload. At the heart of our discovery lies AI-greement, an agent harness for the "autonomous" discovery, implementation, experimentation, and verification of candidate protocols. AI-greement integrates (1) a concept-oriented protocol knowledge base, (2) a modular implementation skeleton, and (3) a Lean-based verification framework with reusable safety definitions, reference specifications, and proofs. AI-greement is of independent interest: its Lean formalization uncovers several previously unreported vulnerabilities in existing consensus protocols, and it provides guidelines on how domain-specific harnesses can turn general-purpose coding agents into effective tools for (distributed) computing research. Yet we argue that human consensus experts remain essential before, during, and after the search: agents reshape the researcher's role rather than end consensus research.
papers.Core_Innovation: Combines lease-authorized local reads, direct client learning for leader-ordered writes, and a topology-aware fixed-quorum per-key write path to eliminate consensus round-trips
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Cloud Computing, Distributed Databases
papers.Decision_Perspective: Pilot A-greement deployment in multi-region key-value stores within 90 days to quantify 30% read-throughput gains. Immediately retire legacy quorum protocols unable to support topology-aware per-key write paths.
papers.Tags: consensus, geo-replication, low-latency, quorum
papers.Hook: AI-designed consensus protocol cuts geo-replicated KV latency by 33.3% across workloads

papers.Title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
papers.Abstract: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period. We introduce Quant-Arena, a benchmark and public leaderboard for end-to-end quantitative research on real A-share market data. A model constructs features and stock-scoring code, receives feedback only on 2022--2023, and freezes one strategy for assessment on the sealed year 2024. A cash-account evaluator applies trading constraints and costs, including market impact estimated from a simulated order book. Scores are dominated by realized excess return and complemented by signal quality and the diversity of features used by the strategy. We evaluate nine frontier models, among which GPT-6 Astra scores highest; yet no model beats the equal-weight market in 2024. Quant-Arena is open to submissions from any model or agent harness.
papers.Core_Innovation: The benchmark freezes strategy selection after iterative feedback on 2022–2023, then assesses on a sealed 2024 year. A cash-account evaluator applies trading constraints, costs, and market impact estimated from a simulated order book.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Quantitative Finance, Algorithmic Trading, Asset Management
papers.Decision_Perspective: Quant teams should integrate Quant-Arena benchmarks into signal development pipelines within 6 months. Firms lacking LLM-quant capabilities should evaluate replacement of legacy research frameworks.
papers.Tags: LLM,Quantitative Trading,Benchmark,A-share,Market Impact
papers.Hook: LLMs now complete end-to-end quantitative research with sealed future evaluation on real A-share data.

papers.Title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
papers.Abstract: We analyze the problem of estimating univariate Gaussian mixture densities using the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) based on $n$ independent and identically distributed samples. We show that the unconstrained NPMLE achieves the minimax optimal rate $\log(n)/n$ in squared Hellinger distance, when the true mixing measure is sub-Gaussian. In addition, we show that when the true mixing measure has compact support, the NMPLE constrained to a compact interval also achieves the minimax optimal rate, which is slightly faster and of order $\log(n)/(n \log \log n)$. Our proof consists of sharply characterizing the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of the class of finite Gaussian mixtures. One of our key technical innovations is to sharply bound the $L^2$ bracketing entropy of balls of bounded-degree polynomials, which may be of independent interest. As an application, we establish the regret-optimality of $g$-modeling procedures based on the NPMLE in the Gaussian Empirical Bayes problem with bounded priors.
papers.Core_Innovation: The proof sharply bounds L2 bracketing entropy of balls of bounded-degree polynomials, enabling precise characterization of local Hellinger bracketing entropy for Gaussian mixture classes.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Finance,Machine Learning
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D budget to integrate NPMLE-based density estimation into risk platforms within 18 months. Retire existing Gaussian mixture tools that lack minimax optimality guarantees.
papers.Tags: gaussian mixtures, nonparametric maximum likelihood, hellinger distance, bracketing entropy, minimax rates
papers.Hook: NPMLE attains minimax optimal rate log(n)/n for sub-Gaussian Gaussian mixtures.

papers.Title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
papers.Abstract: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the current state, Anticipate action effects, Plan a feasible course, Act through an interface or body, and Verify the outcome. Defined by function rather than architecture, these capabilities let PAPAV identify what all three share and then compare MMEAs with MMAs and with RSs. Five physical constraints, from partial observability to unverifiable outcomes, leave fewer choices fixed in advance and less room to reverse errors. Across 64 benchmarks, explicit evaluation centers on Act; only 5 assess Anticipate and 3 assess Verify, leaving both largely hidden behind task success. These constraints also frame the open challenges we identify. PAPAV therefore provides a common basis for designing reliable physical agents and measuring progress across all five capabilities rather than task success alone.
papers.Core_Innovation: PAPAV introduces five architecture-agnostic function-perceptual primitives—Perceive, Anticipate, Plan, Act, Verify—enabling systematic comparison of multimodal embodied agents across computational and robotic domains with explicit physical constraint modeling.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Manufacturing, Logistics, Healthcare
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Conventional Robotics, Static Interface Design
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate capital to prototype PAPAV-integrated robotic systems for high-mix manufacturing by Q2 2026. Discontinue legacy computer-agent projects that lack physical feedback loops.
papers.Tags: Multimodal Embodied Agents,PAPAV,Capability-Centric,Robotics,Computer Agents
papers.Hook: PAPAV unifies multimodal agents across computer and robot domains via five capability functions.

papers.Title: Velocity Ambiguity Profiles: Time-Resolved Bayes-Risk Diagnostics for Flow Matching
papers.Abstract: Flow matching trains a continuum of velocity regression problems but usually reports a loss averaged over interpolation time, obscuring which regions are limited by intrinsic ambiguity and which remain data-limited. We introduce the Velocity Ambiguity Profile (VAP), $\mathcal{A}_v(t)$, the time-local Bayes-risk floor of velocity prediction, and decompose time-resolved loss as $L_N(t)=\mathcal{A}_v(t)+R(t;N)$, where only the excess term $R(t;N)$ is reducible by more data or a different estimator. For $N$ training samples and a $K$-component mixture in the structured example, we prove two statistical benchmarks. In an intrinsic local-regression benchmark, $\mathcal{A}_v(t)$ enters the time-dependent noise factor of the standard nonparametric rate. In separated isotropic Gaussian mixtures, the Bayes velocity becomes locally affine, and a label-oracle residual-regression benchmark has parametric excess-risk scale $K\mathcal{A}_v(t)/N$, matched within the same separated residual Gaussian-location subproblem. Controlled Gaussian-mixture experiments validate this diagnostic through a dense transition sweep, calibrated oracle-to-blind and empirical-proxy audits, and a local controlled time-sampler stress test in which a frozen reducible-error proxy reduces reducible loss while cross-cell sensitivity delimits aggressive sampling. On CIFAR-100 DINOv2 feature flow, guided time sampling reduces uniformly evaluated velocity loss by $6.78\%$ and global feature Fréchet distance (FD) by $23.6\%$, while class-conditional kernel inception distance (KID) shows no improvement. VAP turns an averaged flow-matching objective into a time-resolved diagnostic for locating ambiguity-limited and data-limited regions.
papers.Core_Innovation: The paper introduces the Velocity Ambiguity Profile (VAP), A_v(t), as the time-local Bayes-risk floor of velocity prediction, decomposing time-resolved loss into intrinsic ambiguity and reducible excess risk R(t;N), and proves a parametric excess-risk scale of K*A_v(t)/N for separated isotropic Gaussian mixtures.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: FinTech, Healthcare, Robotics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding to integrate VAP diagnostics into production flow matching pipelines within the next 180 days to quantify data efficiency improvements. Require immediate ambiguity audits on all existing generative models using VAP to identify and target reducible excess risk.
papers.Tags: FlowMatching, VelocityEstimation, BayesRisk, DataEfficiency, GenerativeModels
papers.Hook: Time-resolved ambiguity diagnostics separate intrinsic noise from data-limited error in flow matching

papers.Title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
papers.Abstract: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that a history-conditioned student can learn to do so when trained with on-policy contexts: the student first collects on-policy context under partial observability, and the privileged expert provides action labels conditioned on that context. By distilling expert actions directly conditioned on the student's on-policy history, the student learns to systematically resolve partial observability, i.e., search while uncertain and exploit once the hidden state is revealed. This enables efficient test-time exploration (similar to Bayesian posterior sampling) without incurring the impractical training-data costs of reinforcement learning. Across a diverse range of eleven different environments, including discrete exploration benchmarks, robotic manipulation, navigation, and Procgen environments, ASTEROID achieves ~2x higher returns under fixed exploration budgets, uses ~100x fewer interactions than RL baselines, and outperforms frontier models at exploration. Finally, our method transfers policies trained in simulation to vision-denied real-world robot manipulation, exhibiting efficient exploration and increasing success by +40% over standard distillation. Overall, it provides a simple yet surprisingly effective framework to learn efficient test-time exploration.
papers.Core_Innovation: Students collect on-policy histories under partial observability. Expert action labels are conditioned on those histories, and distillation directly maps student histories to expert actions, enabling systematic partial observability resolution at test time.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Vehicles, Finance
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Traditional Imitation Learning
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund on-policy distillation exploration pilots for autonomous drone swarms within 18 months. Cease procurement of tabula rasa RL platforms unless they achieve ASTEROID-equivalent context-resolution benchmarks.
papers.Tags: POMDP, Imitation Learning, Exploration
papers.Hook: History-conditioned students learn test-time exploration via on-policy expert distillation.

papers.Title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
papers.Abstract: Despite recent advances, current AI systems remain highly susceptible to domain shifts, particularly in biomedical imaging, where images are usually acquired under substantially different experimental conditions. Although recent domain adaptation methods have made substantial progress, significant performance gaps under domain shift persist. To measure progress in this regard, we introduce BatchBench, a leaderboard that evaluates and compares the robustness of AI systems on biomedical images from unseen experimental batches and data sources. BatchBench is built on JUMP-CP, one of the largest publicly available biomedical imaging datasets. Generated using the Cell Painting assay, JUMP-CP exhibits pronounced batch effects and domain shifts, making it a challenging testbed for evaluating robustness to distributional changes.
papers.Core_Innovation: BatchBench enforces batch-disjoint train-test splits across JUMP-CP's Cell Painting experimental conditions, isolating domain shift for rigorous robustness comparison.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Healthcare, Pharmaceuticals, Biotech
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Biomedical AI Vendors, Legacy Diagnostics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Priority should be given to integrating BatchBench validation into biomedical AI product pipelines within the next quarter to ensure domain resilience. Any AI system failing batch-disjoint evaluation must be withdrawn from clinical consideration until retrained.
papers.Tags: BatchBench, DomainShift, BiomedicalImaging, Robustness, CellPainting
papers.Hook: BatchBench standardizes robustness benchmarking for biomedical AI across unseen domains.

papers.Title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
papers.Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) has become a central paradigm for aligning Large Language Models with human values. However, the reliance on sensitive preference data necessitates rigorous differential privacy (DP) guarantees to prevent user information leakage. Existing private alignment methods typically assume dense reward parameterizations, resulting in estimation error bounds that scale polynomially with the ambient {model size $d$}. Such dependence is prohibitive in modern {overparameterized models} where $d$ is vast. In this work, we study \emph{Private Sparse RLHF} problem to address this limitation, assuming that human preferences (reward model) are governed by a subset of $s^* \ll d$ relevant features. We provide the first comprehensive theoretical framework for differentially private sparse reward estimation from pairwise preference feedback under the Bradley-Terry-Luce model, and introduce efficient algorithms for both Sample-DP and Label-DP settings. Theoretically, under the squared $\ell_2$ parameter estimation error, we establish upper bounds of $\widetilde{O}(s^*/n + {s^*}^2/n^2\varepsilon^2)$ for $(\varepsilon,δ)$-Sample-DP and $\widetilde{O}(s^*/n + s^*/n\varepsilon^2)$ for $\varepsilon$-Label-DP based on randomized response, where $n$ is the training data size. For the lower bounds, we show that the Sample-DP rate is nearly optimal, and that the guarantee for our Label-DP method cannot be further improved within the randomized-response framework. We also provide a general lower bound for the problem with Label-DP. Empirically, our framework demonstrates superior efficacy over dense baselines across sentiment generation and safety alignment benchmarks, offering a significantly more favorable privacy-utility trade-off.
papers.Core_Innovation: Introduces sparsity-exploiting DP mechanisms that decouple estimation error from ambient model dimension d under Bradley-Terry-Luce preference feedback
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, LLM Development
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate capital to deploy sparse DP-RLHF pipelines within 18 months for privacy-preserving model alignment. Retire dense-reward DP frameworks incapable of exploiting feature sparsity.
papers.Tags: Differential Privacy, Sparse Rewards, RLHF, Bradley-Terry-Luce
papers.Hook: Differentially private sparse reward estimation now scales independently of massive model dimensions

papers.Title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
papers.Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.
papers.Core_Innovation: SAPO uses semantic-aware gating to block TD residual propagation across atomic task boundaries, isolating credit assignment within subtasks while preserving value bootstrapping
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Manufacturing, Logistics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Imitation Learning, Traditional RL
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate 6-month funding to integrate SAPO into existing VLA post-training pipelines for long-horizon manipulation validation. Phase out IL-only training pipelines that lack atomic task-structure credit-assignment capabilities.
papers.Tags: AtomicRL, Reinforcement Learning, Robotic Manipulation, Semantic Gating, Credit Assignment
papers.Hook: AtomicRL enables precise credit assignment in long-horizon robotic manipulation via semantic task gating

papers.Title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
papers.Abstract: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.
papers.Core_Innovation: Motion and video generation are decoupled, with 3D motion trained on motion-only data and connected to a pretrained video model via lightweight cross-attention, supporting arbitrary skeletons without billion-parameter video models.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Gaming, Film, Visual Effects, Robotics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Motion Capture,Keyframe Animation
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate venture capital to startups integrating cross-attention motion-video pipelines into game engines within 18 months. Retire legacy motion-capture software that cannot support arbitrary-skeleton rigs.
papers.Tags: 3D Motion,Video Generation,Cross-Attention,Arbitrary Rigs
papers.Hook: Co-generates 3D motion and video for arbitrary rigs with registered camera pose.

papers.Title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
papers.Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.
papers.Core_Innovation: Modular LLM-orchestrated agents with dynamic replanning bridge systematic simulations and targeted mechanistic analysis of grain boundaries
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Semiconductor Manufacturing, Aerospace, Energy Storage
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Experimental Metallurgy, Materials Consulting
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding for a 3-month proof-of-concept integrating GBClaw with existing crystal plasticity frameworks. Trigger deployment when internal grain boundary datasets exceed 500 simulated interfaces
papers.Tags: Agentic AI, Grain Boundaries, Mechanistic Discovery, LLM Orchestration, Materials Simulation
papers.Hook: Agentic AI autonomously discovers grain boundary deformation mechanisms at scale

papers.Title: Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills via Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking
papers.Abstract: Dexterous multi-finger hands hold promise to unlock diverse skills like functional grasps, in-hand reorientation, and dynamic handover that the human-designed world assumes, yet existing learning recipes force a trade-off. Goal-reaching reinforcement learning generalizes to arbitrary object poses but, lacking any human prior, converges to unnatural and unreliable finger strategies; motion tracking reproduces human-like behavior from a single clip but cannot deviate from it. We present AdaDex, a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill. At the core of AdaDex is Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking: a shared policy is trained on two populations of massively parallel environments: motion tracking environments trained with dense motion tracking objective, which instill the human prior from human motion; and generalization environments with noised initial states and goals and a sparse object-success reward, which force the skill to work far off the reference. From seconds of human motion per skill, the resulting policies can learn diverse adaptable dexterous skills, such as functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and dynamic behaviors like throw-and-catch. Our method outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality, and we demonstrate transfer across simulators and to the real world. Project page: https://yuxuank.com/AdaDex/.
papers.Core_Innovation: The framework trains a shared policy on two parallel environment populations. One uses dense motion-tracking objectives to embed human motion priors, while the other uses noised goal-conditioned RL for generalization, jointly enabling adaptable dexterous skills from sparse trajectories.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Manufacturing, Logistics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Motion Capture, Rigid Automation
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding for AdaDex integration pilots in high-precision manufacturing within 12 months. Retire legacy motion-capture-dependent animation workflows within 6 months that cannot generalize beyond fixed clips.
papers.Tags: Dexterous Manipulation, Goal-Conditioned RL, Hybrid Mimicking
papers.Hook: Sparse human motion clips enable fully adaptable dexterous manipulation.

papers.Title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
papers.Abstract: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).
papers.Core_Innovation: UniWALM embeds video, action, and language into a single Mixture-of-Transformers backbone with synchronized diffusion heads that co-denoise jointly, recursively consuming generated text as memory to eliminate separate planning stages.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Manufacturing, Logistics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Modular Planning Systems
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund university labs to prototype UniWALM-integrated manipulators within 18 months. Acquire or partner with teams deploying synchronous multimodal diffusion architectures for real-time embodied control.
papers.Tags: multimodal, embodied robotics, diffusion, language memory, mixture-of-transformers
papers.Hook: Unified model jointly generates action, language, and memory for embodied control without separate planning.

papers.Title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
papers.Abstract: Warehouse robot fleets continuously observe operational conditions, but preserving these observations as reusable semantic memory incurs substantial computation, communication, and storage costs. For example, explaining recurring aisle blockages can require reviewing video from multiple robots across several shifts. We present IndustrialRemembr, a shared spatiotemporal memory system that extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR to robot fleets and reduces server-side computation by generating scene descriptions only on demand. On each robot, an NVIDIA Jetson encodes video clips into retrieval embeddings with Cosmos-Embed1, vision tokens with Cosmos3-Edge, and reconstruction latents with the Wan2.2 VAE, without uploading raw camera frames. The encoding models are re-used to detect people in image patches, zeroing them out to support PII abstraction for GDPR-compliant deployments. We split Cosmos3-Edge at its vision-language boundary, placing the vision encoder on the robot and the language decoder on an on-premises server. A Nemotron agent retrieves memories by content, position, and time and queries the decoder using cached vision tokens. This design eliminates caption generation at write time, while cached-token decoding reproduces the unsplit model's output in all 450 tested decodes.
papers.Core_Innovation: Splitting the vision-language model at its boundary places the vision encoder on resource-constrained robots while offloading the language decoder to servers, enabling on-demand scene description without raw video transmission.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Warehousing, Logistics, Robotics, Manufacturing
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Cloud Video Analytics, Traditional Surveillance
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding to integrate on-edge VLM pipelines into existing robot fleets within 12 months, triggered by automation ROI thresholds. Phase out raw-video-upload surveillance systems in favor of on-demand scene description architectures.
papers.Tags: Edge Computing, Computer Vision, Robotics, Memory Systems, PII Abstraction
papers.Hook: Robot fleets compress video on-device, uploading only scene descriptions on demand.

papers.Title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
papers.Abstract: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. At the highest tested noise level in 4D, PUN achieves 10.7-60.6% relative gains in success rate over other methods while running 3.29-32.15 times faster.
papers.Core_Innovation: Reflecting Neumann boundary conditions on obstacles replace Dirichlet termination, preserving goal signals across long free-space paths. Neural operators then approximate these noise-aware value fields in higher-dimensional PDEs without configuration-space meshes.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Vehicles, Aerospace Simulation, Game AI
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Traditional Motion Planning, Mesh-Based Solvers
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D budget to prototype PUN-based planners on robotic platforms within 12 months. Evaluate performance against state-of-the-art mesh-free solvers in standardized obstacle courses.
papers.Tags: Neural Operators, Stochastic Optimal Control, Boundary Conditions, Monte Carlo Planning
papers.Hook: Neural operators enable real-time planning in unseen geometries under execution noise.

papers.Title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
papers.Abstract: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.
papers.Core_Innovation: MindView introduces a dual-family task taxonomy separating geometry-dominant camera-pose changes from semantics-dominant object-grounding challenges. Paired-context testing then shows all evaluated generators perform worse with expanded multi-view observations
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Augmented Reality, Autonomous Vehicles
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding for task-specific generative model development targeting MindView geometry-dominant tasks within 18 months. Phase out generic multi-view generators that underperform on paired-context robustness evaluations
papers.Tags: Generative AI, Multi-View Spatial Intelligence, Benchmark Evaluation, Context Robustness
papers.Hook: New benchmark enables generative multi-view spatial intelligence evaluation across geometry and semantics tasks

papers.Title: Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction: How far should we go?
papers.Abstract: Multi-token prediction (MTP) can accelerate language-model decoding by drafting several tokens and verifying them in a single target-model pass. However, the best speculation horizon changes with context: longer drafts offer greater amortization when reliable, but can waste compute on suffixes discarded after a rejection. Unlike autoregressive drafting, where a stopping rule can decide token by token, MTP must fix the horizon before drafting, as all heads fire in the same forward pass. We therefore formulate horizon selection as an online control problem, using verification feedback to learn how far the draft can be trusted in each context, and introduce Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP): a lightweight controller that requires no retraining and leaves the exact verifier unchanged. To guide horizon selection, we characterize the expected number of tokens committed at each horizon via acceptance survival, the probability that a draft prefix is fully accepted. Before each round, AMTP predicts how far the draft is likely to survive and picks the horizon with the highest expected tokens per second, learning freely from every verification pass. Theoretically, we show that any online learner's prediction error translates into throughput regret against the best horizon for each context, and in turn into a bound on wall-clock completion time. With online gradient descent, this regret is sublinear. Across five draft-target pairings built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Medusa heads, Meta's MTP models, and Qwen3-4B-Inst-2507-MTP, evaluated on AIME 2025 and GSM8K, AMTP decodes up to 4.1x faster than standard decoding and matches or outperforms the fixed window in 8 of 10 settings, with throughput gains of up to 10%.
papers.Core_Innovation: AMTP formulates horizon selection as an online control problem using verification feedback. It computes per-context acceptance survival probabilities before each drafting round without retraining or verifier modification.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Large Language Model Providers, Cloud Services, Developer Tools
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Traditional Autoregressive LLM Serving, Static Drafting Workflows
papers.Decision_Perspective: AI labs should allocate engineering resources to integrate AMTP into decoding pipelines within the next two quarters to realize compute savings. Organizations using fixed-horizon MTP should transition to adaptive controllers before major model version upgrades.
papers.Tags: MTP, Adaptive Control, LLM Decoding
papers.Hook: Context-adaptive drafting horizon enables compute-optimal LLM decoding without retraining.

papers.Title: Efficient Edge-aware Attention Network for Graph Generation
papers.Abstract: Graph generative models commonly use graph-specific Transformer architectures to jointly update node and edge features. However, these architectures do not directly benefit from recent hardware-aware attention implementations, limiting their scalability. The adaptation is, however, non-trivial: edge and graph-level features must be injected into pairwise attention scores, graph masks must be respected, and dynamic edge updates remain a major source of quadratic memory usage. We propose an edge-aware attention layer for graph generation that incorporates structural information through head-wise score modulation, while updating edge representations with a lightweight residual mechanism that retains attention-score dependent edge updates. This layer can be effectively implemented using PyTorch's FlexAttention. We achieve similar generation quality to our baseline while reducing peak GPU memory by around 65% and substantially improving training and sampling throughput. These results suggest that the proposed architecture is a practical step toward scalable graph foundation models.
papers.Core_Innovation: Head-wise score modulation embeds structural priors into attention weights. A lightweight residual update preserves attention-score-dependent edge gradients.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Pharmaceuticals, Semiconductor Design, Social Media Analytics
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: High-Memory Graph Transformer Implementations
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund development of FlexAttention-integrated graph generators within 12 months to capture 65% memory savings. Phase out high-memory graph Transformer pilots exceeding 40% GPU overhead.
papers.Tags: Graph Attention, FlexAttention, Memory Efficiency, Generative Modeling, Edge Representation
papers.Hook: Hardware-aware graph attention now possible with edge-aware score modulation.

papers.Title: Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics
papers.Abstract: Modern distributed microservice deployments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous, multi-format observability logs across physically and logically partitioned infrastructure. Isolating root causes during cascading failures remains an arduous task for Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), bottlenecked by manual keyword filtering and disjointed temporal correlation across monitoring dashboards. We introduce Semantic Observability, an autonomous multi-agent framework that unifies disparate log streams into a dynamic, queryable Property Graph Database. By modeling physical infrastructure topologies, logical software dependencies, and chronological event sequences as attributed nodes and directed relations, it bridges the semantic gap inherent in flat, unstructured log repositories. Building on this unified substrate, we deploy a stateful multi-agent system orchestrated through Directed Cyclic Graphs (DCGs). The system autonomously navigates the topology, applying causal graph algorithms and temporal back-traversal to isolate the precise blast radius of anomalies. The pruned subgraph is then interpreted by a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning engine to generate contextualized, code-level Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and actionable remediations. This paper establishes the foundational system architecture, formal relational ontology, and multi-agent control loops of Semantic Observability. We show conceptually how the framework eliminates ambient telemetry noise, reduces Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), compresses LLM token consumption, and prevents structural hallucinations. We also specify an open-source validation framework on standard benchmarks (LogHub and Train-Ticket), laying the groundwork for a forthcoming companion paper on exhaustive quantitative evaluation and production benchmarking.
papers.Core_Innovation: It converts heterogeneous, unstructured observability logs into an attributed property graph modeling physical topologies, logical dependencies, and event sequences, then runs a Directed Cyclic Graph-orchestrated multi-agent system for autonomous causal root-cause isolation.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Cloud Computing, Financial Services, E-commerce
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy Observability Platforms, Manual SRE Tooling
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate capital to semantic graph observability prototypes within 18 months to achieve autonomous root-cause isolation. Phase out legacy keyword-filtering monitoring vendors rendered obsolete by this framework.
papers.Tags: semantic observability, multi-agent systems, property graph, causal inference
papers.Hook: Agents diagnose cascading failures via unified property graphs in real time.

papers.Title: Benchmarking Arabic Dialects for Math Problems
papers.Abstract: Mathematical reasoning remains underexplored for low-resource languages, including Dialectal Arabic. To bridge this gap, we introduce the DAR-MGSM (Dialectal Arabic Multilingual Grade School Math) Benchmark, the first manually curated benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in Dialectal Arabic. DAR-MGSM consists of math word problems (MWPs) requiring multi-step reasoning and covers five major Arabic dialects alongside Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). The benchmark comprises two parallel versions: translated-only and translated & culturally localized. The latter version adapts entities and references to regional varieties. We evaluate eleven Arabic-centric and multilingual large language models on DAR-MGSM. The results show that the performance generally declines on the localized version, highlighting the challenges introduced by culturally grounded adaptations. However, the magnitude of this effect varies across models, with Arabic-centric models exhibiting different levels of sensitivity to localization. A mechanistic interpretability analysis shows that translated and localized variants of the same MWPs often induce distinct internal reasoning trajectories, even when aggregate accuracy remains similar. Overall, our results show that mathematical reasoning performance depends on both linguistic variety and cultural context.
papers.Core_Innovation: DAR-MGSM introduces parallel translated-only and culturally localized benchmark variants to isolate dialect and cultural effects on Arabic LLM math reasoning.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: EdTech, Artificial Intelligence, Language Technology
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Generic AI, Standardized EdTech
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate Q1 2027 funding for Arabic LLM teams to integrate DAR-MGSM cultural localization metrics into multi-step math reasoning pipelines. Deprecate generic math tutoring deployments that lack dialectal adaptation benchmarks.
papers.Tags: ArabicDialects, MathReasoning, LLMBenchmark, CulturalLocalization, LowResource
papers.Hook: First benchmark enables math reasoning evaluation across Arabic dialects and cultural localization.

papers.Title: Value-Rich, Differently Organized: Measuring Value Expression and Organization in AI-Generated Debates
papers.Abstract: Current evaluation of LLM-generated debate largely focuses on argumentative quality, leaving the value structure of generated arguments underexamined. We introduce a diagnostic metric framework for comparing how values are expressed and organized in human-reference and AI-generated debates. The framework separates value expression, the range of recognizable values a debate invokes, from value organization, how those values are distributed and sustained across turns. Grounded in Schwartz's Basic-10 value theory, it represents debates as multi-level value distributions over argumentative units, utterances, stances, and full debates, enabling metrics for value coverage, alignment, diffusion, and cross-turn dynamics. Across multiple generation systems, AI-generated debates are broadly value-expressive, often activating as many or more value dimensions than matched human references, but they organize these values differently. Their utterances are more locally value-diffuse, and source-blind judges distinguish value clarity from value focus. These findings show that debate evaluation should consider not only value presence, but also value organization. Code and supplementary materials are available at https://github.com/Maoyuan-li/Value-Expression-and-Organization.
papers.Core_Innovation: The framework computes value expression as the range of recognizable values and value organization as their distribution across turns, using Schwartz's Basic-10 theory to model debates as multi-level distributions over argumentative units, utterances, stances, and full debates.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Political Analysis
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Human Debate Coaching, Traditional Media Monitoring
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding to integrate value-expression/organization metrics into LLM deployment pipelines within the next 90 days. Discontinue manual sentiment audits that lack source-blind cross-turn diffusion capabilities.
papers.Tags: Value Expression, Value Organization, Schwartz Theory, LLM Debates, Multi-level Distribution
papers.Hook: A framework quantifies how AI debates express and organize distinct human values across turns.

papers.Title: Turning TS2Vec into a Foundation Model for Time Series Classification
papers.Abstract: TS2Vec is one of the strongest self-supervised methods for time series classification, introduced in 2022. It is designed to be trained anew on every dataset: self-supervised pre-training followed by linear probing. Since then, the field has shifted towards foundation models that reuse one encoder across datasets. Yet TS2Vec offers a compact convolutional architecture that operates directly on temporal samples and accepts variable-length inputs without resampling. We ask whether these properties can be retained when the encoder is pre-trained only once, and show that they can: TS2Vec can essentially be turned into a foundation model. Three changes suffice: pre-train on a synthetic corpus, feed the encoder a raw amplitude view and an instance-normalized shape view of the input through two small stems, and distill one specialist encoder per view into a single encoder. The result, TS2Vec-FM, is a 1.6M-parameter dilated convolutional network that, kept frozen, reaches 83.3% on UCR-128 and 75.3% on UEA-27 under linear probing, within 0.3 pp of MantisV2, the current state of the art, and above TS2Vec trained separately on each target dataset. What we find most interesting is how different TS2Vec-FM is from other foundation models in design: near-parity is reached without attention, without a patch tokenizer, and without intermediate-layer extraction, using an "old-school" convolutional encoder and a two-layer MLP stem.
papers.Core_Innovation: A dual-stem encoder simultaneously ingests raw amplitude and instance-normalized shape views, then distills them into one frozen dilated convolutional backbone.

papers.Hook: One pre-training turns TS2Vec into a frozen foundation model for variable-length time series.

papers.Title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
papers.Abstract: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models. We argue that interface design should itself be an agent capability. We introduce Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that builds Evolving Agent Interfaces from task experience. A meta-agent examines task agents' trajectories on synthetic training tasks, without success labels, and constructs and revises interfaces and usage knowledge in a repository. Population-based evolution then selects which repositories to develop further by their performance on validation tasks the meta-agent never sees, favoring changes that generalize beyond the seen tasks. On OSWorld V2, Agent S4, with Qwen3.8-27B and the evolved repository of interfaces, sets a new state of the art in open-source computer-use agents, reaching 21.3% binary score, 3.8 times the same model with fixed interfaces. This is above both GPT-5.5 (13.0%) and Claude Opus 4.8 (20.6%), at about 4.3% and 1.5% of their respective costs. On ScienceBoard, the evolved interfaces improve the success rate from 41.4% to 58.6% with the same model. These results suggest that useful interfaces can be evolved from experience, making autonomous interface design a source of improvement complementary to advances in models and harnesses. We open-source our code at https://github.com/simular-ai/agent-s.
papers.Core_Innovation: Replaces static, hand-coded API/UI mappings with a meta-agent that evolves interface repositories via population-based selection based on trajectory efficiency.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Enterprise Software, Robotic Process Automation, Cloud Infrastructure
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: UI/UX Design, Manual QA Testing
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund startups building self-optimizing middleware that abstracts legacy software interfaces for LLM agents. Kill investments in static RPA tools that rely on fixed selector-based automation by Q4 2026.
papers.Tags: Agentic Workflows, Meta-Learning, Interface Evolution, OSWorld
papers.Hook: Agents can now autonomously design and evolve their own software interfaces to optimize task execution.

papers.Title: Neural Implicit Energy Optimization for LiDAR Mapping
papers.Abstract: Neural implicit representations provide memory-efficient signed distance field (SDF) parameterizations for large-scale LiDAR scenes, but the geometry recovered from sparse and often noisy inputs carries jitter and artifacts. Classical geometric optimization techniques resolve such artifacts with surface energy functionals, whose minimizers correspond to smooth surfaces. Motivated by this principle, we formulate neural LiDAR mapping as the optimization of energy functionals over the parameter space of neural implicit representations. Specifically, we regularize the signed distance field with an energy functional defined on the shape operator of its level set, which represents the curvature of the surface, thus encouraging smoothness along the surface. This adapts classical geometric priors to the scale of million-point LiDAR maps. Experiments on large-scale datasets show reconstructions with improved smoothness at preserved geometric fidelity, and no additional inference-time cost. The code is publicly available at \href{https://github.com/HrishikeshVish/nieo}{https://github.com/HrishikeshVish/nieo}
papers.Core_Innovation: They introduce an energy functional defined on the shape operator of neural implicit level sets, embedding curvature-based smoothness priors directly into the optimization of signed distance fields for LiDAR mapping.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Autonomous Vehicles, Robotics, Geospatial Mapping
papers.Decision_Perspective: Autonomous vehicle teams should integrate shape-operator regularization into LiDAR mapping pipelines within the next 12 months to achieve smoother reconstructions without computational overhead. Competitors relying on classical mesh smoothing should benchmark this method against their pipelines within 3 months to assess viability.
papers.Tags: Neural Implicit, LiDAR Mapping, Curvature Regularization, Geometric Optimization, Signed Distance Field
papers.Hook: Curvature-regularized neural SDFs enable smooth large-scale LiDAR mapping with zero inference cost

papers.Title: What Do RTL Repair Benchmarks Actually Measure?
papers.Abstract: RTL repair benchmarks should measure whether a model can fix broken RTL given a specification. To this end, we construct and hash-bind RTLRepairDataset, 5,784 (broken, fixed) training pairs; RTLRepairBench, 459 held-out cases with 374 syntactic and 85 behavioral mutations; and an evaluation harness supporting simulation and formal equivalence. We then use this infrastructure to identify two measurement confounds. First, simulation and formal scoring give opposite signs for the apparent effect of providing a specification in one evaluated cohort; reset-aware rescoring attributes almost all of the simulation-formal disagreement to reset and first-cycle comparison semantics. Second, on 274 mined model failures, the specification-only minus specification-conditioned recovery point estimate ranges from -8.5 to +18.3 percentage points across six models. Thus, a conventional repair score need not isolate whether the model used the faulty RTL. We translate these findings into evaluation controls: report initialization, reset, first-cycle, and unknown-value semantics; disclose oracle coverage and undecided cases; and include a specification-only baseline. Together, the resources and audit provide both a benchmark for behavioral repair and a protocol for diagnosing what contributes to its measured score. We release the benchmark, the training set, construction code, sanitized aggregate evidence, and reproduction materials at https://github.com/Evaaaz/RTLRepairBench.
papers.Core_Innovation: Reset-aware rescoring attributes simulation-formal scoring disagreement to first-cycle comparison semantics, not specification efficacy. Empirical ranges show specification presence need not indicate whether models engaged the faulty RTL.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Semiconductor Design, Electronic Design Automation, Verification
papers.Decision_Perspective: Chip vendors must replace simulation-only repair scores with reset-aware formal equivalence pipelines within 12 months. EDA toolmakers are required to integrate first-cycle comparison semantics to prevent metric contamination.
papers.Tags: RTL Repair, Benchmarking, Formal Methods, Semiconductor
papers.Hook: Reset-aware rescoring isolates model engagement with faulty RTL from first-cycle semantics.

papers.Title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
papers.Abstract: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.
papers.Core_Innovation: MFlow introduces a learnable, data‑dependent mixing coefficient that interpolates between clean‑image (x0) and velocity (u) prediction along the principal axes of the data distribution, trained jointly with the diffusion objective. This allows the model to automatically select the optimal parameterization per direction, shifting toward velocity prediction as model capacity grows.
